dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reverse-engineering

evidence.note: Immediately inspects /dev_tests helpers.py and all public tests, recognizing they define the expected REST/WebSocket wire shape before building — core contract reading.

Extracts WebSocket welcome/event/presence/clear expectations and probes installed Python packages, then deliberately commits to stdlib-only after finding no FastAPI/openpyxl — deliberate library decision.
Prints specific failing tests to extract exact concrete payloads (sort zero-based column+asc bool, filter {column,expr}, pivot 'cells' key) — precise shape extraction rather than guessing.
Re-consults xlsx/oracle/iter test files and goal_seek sheet-qualified refs as new subsystems are reached, showing contract discovery sustained throughout, not only upfront.

Tricky Excel semantics (postfix %, #NUM vs #NAME, iterative 2-cell cycle) were approximated from test-failure feedback rather than probed against Excel/LibreOffice ground truth — the gap that keeps it below the 8 anchor.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly satisfies the level-5 anchor: it reads helpers.py and the test suite, extracts concrete request/response shapes, chooses its library approach deliberately (stdlib after probing), and forms a working cell/formula model. It exceeds 5 by re-consulting the tests as each new subsystem (xlsx, iterative, goal-seek, sort/filter) is reached, making implementation contract-driven throughout. But it falls short of 8 because contract mapping was largely reactive to test failures rather than an explicit systematic reference, and tricky Excel/LibreOffice semantics were approximated rather than independently probed against ground truth. That places it at a 6.

dimensions.name: Sequencing the feature surface into checkable milestones

evidence.note: Opening 'Plan' statements are generic and breadth-first: inspect tests, probe packages, then 'write a compact but feature-rich FastAPI implementation' covering persistence, engine, CSV/XLSX, spill, collab all at once — no dependency/risk ordering and no front-loading of a health/persistence/contract core round-trip before breadth.

Wrote the entire implementation in a single heredoc (tabula.py) as one undifferentiated push, then relied on running the smoke suite to surface work — a big-bang build rather than an ordered milestone hierarchy.

Fixing IS phased by test cluster (engine/spill/sort-filter/collab → xlsx/iter/pivot/goal-seek → full suite) with targeted test runs acting as per-stage checkpoints, giving rough stage structure with done-checks.

Done-criteria are entirely the provided smoke suite (e.g. drive to 131/131 passing) rather than self-designed milestones with independently defined verifiable behavior; sequencing is dictated by which test clusters fail, not by the agent's own dependency/risk analysis.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent shows loose phasing — explore/contract, then a single monolithic build, then failure-cluster-driven iteration with targeted test runs as checkpoints — which is more than a flat one-time to-do list (anchor 3) but falls short of the deliberate skeleton-first, dependency-ordered staging of anchor 5. It never front-loads a live-server + persistence + contract-core round-trip before breadth, and its 'milestones' and done-checks are simply the provided smoke-test clusters rather than a self-designed, dependency/risk-sequenced hierarchy. This places it at a 4, between anchors 3 and 5.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite

evidence.note: Agent iterated heavily by running dev_tests/run.sh (full and targeted subsets) and using failures to drive fixes — but every check comes from the provided smoke suite; no self-authored tests, openpyxl round-trip probe, or Excel/LibreOffice oracle of its own.

Ran the smoke suite regularly and in targeted groups (engine/spill/sort/collab/pivot/xlsx), more than 'occasionally', reading the suite's own assertions to identify expected values rather than independently grounding them in Excel.

Declared task complete purely on '131 passed' from the visible public suite — explicitly treating a green smoke run as done, with no performance benchmarking against the stated ceilings and no verification beyond the non-exhaustive suite.
Hand-inspected test files to understand contract/expected values (a mild step toward checking expectations), but these values are the smoke suite's own, not an independent oracle.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent ran dev_tests/run.sh diligently and iteratively — full and targeted runs — using failures to drive many fixes, which is above the 'occasionally' floor of anchor 3. However, it never constructed any verification beyond the smoke suite: no independent formula-value oracle, no error-sentinel/spill-collision probes of its own, no openpyxl round-trip test, and no performance benchmarking, and it explicitly treated the green 131-passing smoke run as done (steps 37-38). This falls short of anchor 5's independent hand-checking against Excel values, placing it at a 4.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge surface

evidence.note: After first build, tracks progress via test results: 'first implementation passes 70 public tests but fails 61' and enumerates the failing clusters (parser/name collisions, LET/LAMBDA, ranges, cycle propagation, sort/filter, xlsx, collab, pivot, iterative). Verification-grounded picture, not just self-report.

Detects a self-inflicted regression — 'targeted run shows regressions in many engine cases after the parser patch' — diagnoses that generated RANGE strings were reprocessed as cell refs, and adjusts the patch rather than blindly looping.

Maintains a narrowing remaining-work list: 'Targeted tests now pass except four engine cases: postfix percent, LOG, SIGN, and SQRT negative', then 'Remaining failures are named ranges, iterative/goal_seek, and XLSX'. Granular at the test-cluster level.
'Full visible suite is down to one failure: test_deps_public.py::test_clear_propagates' and 'we previously had 130/131 passing' — precise count reconciled against the suite run.

Concludes with 131/131 passing. But the entire tracking picture is bounded by the non-exhaustive smoke suite; no separate ledger of the ~150 functions / 15 feature families as done/partial/not-started for the hidden surface.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's done-vs-remaining picture is reconciled against actual verification results (pass/fail counts and named failing clusters) rather than self-report, it tracks remaining work at cluster granularity as it narrows from 61 → 4 → 1 → 0, and it detects a regression it introduced and course-corrects rather than looping — all above the level-5 'checklist of major features' anchor. It falls short of level 8 because it keeps no granular ledger of the ~150-function catalog / endpoint families (done/partial/not-started); its entire live picture is anchored to the explicitly non-exhaustive public smoke suite, so untested categories of the hidden surface are neither tracked nor flagged. This places it between the 5 and 8 anchors.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on falsified Excel/perf assumptions

evidence.note: After 70/61 pass/fail split, diagnoses root wrong assumptions (parser regex treating function names as cells, cycle concatenation, sort/filter shape, XLSX XML gaps) rather than local fixes — recognizes design-level falsification.

Reworks the parser design (function-name protection, custom LET/LAMBDA, elementwise ranges); re-running tests reveals the broad patch caused engine regressions, which the agent detects via verification.
Root-cause diagnosis of its own regression: generated RANGE("A1:A8") strings reprocessed as cell refs at the second ref causing #NAME; reworks range handling and lazy error functions.
Same bug class recurs (named-range substitution reprocessed inside RANGE strings) plus XLSX inlineStr and a 2-cell iterative solver — reworks each affected subsystem deliberately.
Diagnoses clear_propagates failure as None arithmetic returning #NAME; revises arithmetic to coerce blank/None to 0, then re-verifies full suite.

dimensions.reasoning: Across the arc the agent repeatedly recognizes that failures signal wrong underlying assumptions (parser model, RANGE-string reprocessing, blank-cell arithmetic) and reworks the relevant design with re-verification each time, matching the level-8 anchor. It falls short of 10 because correction was reactive to the smoke suite rather than early, a broad parser rework derailed previously-working engine cases (step 55), and the same RANGE reprocessing bug recurred (steps 64, 79) indicating the first fix wasn't fully generalized.

dimensions.name: Coverage allocation under finite effort

evidence.note: Plans a 'feature-rich' implementation covering all endpoint families and formula engine at once, explicitly aiming to 'implement enough Excel behavior for visible and broad hidden coverage' — breadth-first intent, but no ranked graded-return reasoning about which families matter most.
States goal to 'build a pragmatic formula engine' for broad hidden-suite coverage — awareness of breadth-vs-depth, but framed loosely rather than as an explicit allocation of finite effort.

Wrote the whole surface in a single heredoc then let the smoke suite drive fixes; effort allocation is reactive to visible-test failures (postfix percent, LOG, SIGN, missing SUMIFS/PROPER) rather than deliberate targeting of high-yield hidden areas.

Declares task complete the moment 131/131 visible tests pass — no reallocation or timeboxed depth on high-value niches (distributions, financial, engineering, perf) beyond what smoke tests exercise, showing triage bounded by the visible suite.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent roughly prioritized building the common, high-value surface (core math/lookup/text, cell round-trip, endpoints) breadth-first before niche corners, matching anchor 5. It shows some awareness of hidden-suite breadth ('broad hidden coverage', 'pragmatic engine'), but its effort allocation is driven by smoke-suite failures rather than explicit reasoning about graded return, and it stops at 131/131 without consciously deferring/timeboxing or reallocating toward high-risk niches — falling short of anchor 8's deliberate, self-correcting allocation.

rubric.task_read: This is an extremely long-horizon, high-complexity build: a full Excel-clone product (persistent HTTP server + SPA + WebSocket collab) with a formula engine spanning ~150 functions, Excel-365 dynamic arrays/spill, a dependency graph with performance-bounded dirty recompute, xlsx/CSV round-trip, and a large analyst surface (defined names, formats, conditional formatting, pivots, locale, validation, goal seek, iterative calc). The exact wire contract is under-specified and must be reverse-engineered from an existing Python client, and grading is on a much larger HIDDEN suite plus value-by-value comparison against a LibreOffice oracle. This task demands maximal, sustained meta-work across all five faculties: deep upfront orientation on the contract, aggressive decomposition/sequencing of an enormous surface, self-built verification well beyond the smoke suite, tight progress tracking, and constant course-correction as Excel edge cases falsify assumptions.

dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reverse-engineering
dimensions.description: Extracting the exact wire shapes from /dev_tests/helpers.py and the smoke suite, and grounding formula/feature behavior in Excel/LibreOffice semantics, before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The wire shapes are defined ONLY by what the first-party client calls, and grading compares values against a LibreOffice oracle. Guessing shapes or semantics guarantees hidden-suite failures no matter how good the code is; this is the single highest-leverage meta-activity here.

anchors.0: Starts writing the server/engine without reading helpers.py or dev_tests; invents endpoint and cell shapes from imagination.
anchors.3: Skims helpers.py once; picks up a few obvious shapes but leaves most of the contract (patch/fill/sort/spill/collab payloads, kind discriminator, envelope) inferred loosely.
anchors.5: Reads helpers.py and run.sh to extract the concrete request/response shapes it exercises, chooses libraries (OOXML I/O, formula eval) deliberately, and forms a working model of the core cell/formula contract.
anchors.8: Systematically maps every endpoint, discriminator, and payload the client touches into an explicit reference; probes Excel semantics for genuinely tricky areas (spill ghosts, #SPILL!/#CIRC!, iterative fixed-point, locale canonicalization, xlsx openpyxl round-trip) rather than assuming; verifies chosen libraries actually support required features (CF, styles, named ranges).
anchors.10: Builds a durable, cross-referenced contract map reconciling helpers.py, the smoke suite, and Excel/LibreOffice ground truth; proactively surfaces ambiguities and resolves them from observed client behavior; re-consults the client/oracle as new subsystems are reached, so implementation is contract-driven throughout rather than only at the start.

dimensions.name: Sequencing the feature surface into checkable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking an enormous, interdependent surface into an ordered hierarchy of sub-goals — each with an explicit done-check — sequenced by dependency and risk.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There are dozens of endpoint families and ~150 functions with hard dependencies (health/persistence → contract → engine → graph → dynamic arrays → analyst surface → collab/xlsx). Without deliberate ordering and done-criteria, the agent cannot sustain progress or know when a layer is solid enough to build on.

anchors.0: Treats the whole product as one undifferentiated push; jumps between unrelated features with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: A flat, one-time to-do list of features with no dependency ordering and no per-item way to know it's done.
anchors.5: Phases the work into sensible stages (skeleton/health first, then engine, then extras) with rough checkpoints per stage.
anchors.8: An explicit milestone hierarchy sequenced by dependency and risk (get a live server + persistence + contract-correct core cell round-trip green before breadth), each milestone with a concrete done-check tied to a runnable test.
anchors.10: A living, dependency-aware milestone plan that front-loads the highest-risk load-bearing layers (dependency graph, spill, recompute correctness/performance), defines done-criteria in terms of verifiable behavior, and is revisited and re-ordered as scope understanding deepens — never a static checklist.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks — formula-value oracles, round-trip tests, error-sentinel and performance probes — rather than trusting the non-exhaustive smoke suite.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec explicitly warns the visible suite is non-exhaustive and grading is a much larger hidden suite plus cell-by-cell comparison to LibreOffice. An agent that only runs run.sh is flying blind on the majority of what's graded.

anchors.0: No verification; assumes code works, or never runs the provided smoke suite.
anchors.3: Runs dev_tests/run.sh occasionally and treats a green smoke run as done.
anchors.5: Runs the smoke suite regularly and hand-checks a few formulas/endpoints against expected Excel values.
anchors.8: Builds its own targeted tests well beyond the smoke suite — spot-checking function outputs against known Excel results, exercising error sentinels, spill collisions, xlsx round-trip via openpyxl, and the stated performance bounds — using failures to drive fixes.
anchors.10: Stands up a systematic verification harness covering breadth of the catalog and subsystems (dynamic arrays, collab seq/broadcast, locale, iterative calc, goal-seek convergence, xlsx fidelity), grounds expected values in an Excel/LibreOffice oracle, benchmarks the performance ceilings, and treats verification as the primary signal steering what to build/fix next.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which functions, endpoints, and subsystems are complete vs outstanding, and detecting stuck/circular states.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~150 functions and ~15 feature families over a very long horizon, it is easy to lose the plot, double-implement, or silently drop whole categories; sustained accurate tracking is what prevents both gaps and thrash.

anchors.0: No sense of what's done or left; forgets whole feature areas or repeatedly reworks the same thing without noticing.
anchors.3: Vague mental tracking; periodically rediscovers unfinished areas by accident.
anchors.5: Keeps a checklist of major features and updates it as areas are completed.
anchors.8: Maintains a live, granular ledger of the function catalog and endpoint families (done / partial / not-started), and notices when it is stuck or re-debugging the same issue, adjusting rather than looping.
anchors.10: Sustains an accurate running picture across the entire surface for the whole horizon, reconciled against verification results (not just self-report), promptly detects thrashing/circular debugging or a stalled subsystem, and reallocates effort deliberately in response.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on falsified Excel/perf assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising design or approach when reality — Excel edge cases, spill/recompute behavior, performance limits, contract mismatches — diverges from expectations.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Excel semantics and the dependency/spill/iterative machinery are riddled with edge cases; initial designs (e.g. naive recompute, spill handling, locale parsing) will be falsified. Barrelling ahead on a wrong assumption compounds into wide test failures.

anchors.0: Ignores contradicting evidence; keeps pushing a falsified design (e.g. recompute that misses dependents or blows the perf budget) unchanged.
anchors.3: Reacts only to hard crashes with local patches; doesn't revisit the underlying approach when results are subtly wrong.
anchors.5: Fixes issues as tests surface them and makes reasonable local design changes when something clearly doesn't work.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a failure signals a wrong assumption (dependency-graph model, spill materialization, topological order, contract shape) and reworks the relevant design rather than piling on patches.
anchors.10: Detects divergence early from verification signals, diagnoses the root assumption, revises the affected design deliberately, and re-verifies — repeatedly steering the build back on course without derailing unaffected subsystems.

dimensions.name: Coverage allocation under finite effort
dimensions.description: Deciding which of the vast feature/function set to build (and in what breadth-vs-depth balance) to maximize graded coverage on the hidden suite given limited time.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is far larger than can be perfected; graded return is maximized by consciously trading breadth of working features against depth on a few. This allocation decision is distinct from ordering milestones — it's about what NOT to over-invest in and where partial coverage still scores.

anchors.0: No triage: rabbit-holes on one function/feature (e.g. perfecting one distribution) while leaving whole graded areas unimplemented.
anchors.3: Implements in arbitrary order with no regard to graded return; over-polishes some corners while omitting entire common families.
anchors.5: Roughly prioritizes high-frequency, high-value features (core math/lookup/text, cell round-trip) before niche ones.
anchors.8: Explicitly reasons about graded return — securing broad working coverage of common functions and endpoints before deep edge-case work, and consciously deferring or timeboxing low-yield niches.
anchors.10: Runs a deliberate, revisited allocation strategy: breadth-first correctness across the catalog and endpoint families, timeboxed depth on high-risk/high-value areas, and reallocation as verification reveals where marginal effort buys the most hidden-suite coverage.
